title: Irreducibility of an affine linear incidence hypersurface
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] which is an integral domain. Let $r\geq1$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$, with at least one $f_i\ne0$. Set $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. Assume every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ minimal among those containing $J$ has height at least two. Here height is the supremum of lengths of chains of prime ideals ending at $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; when $J=A$ the condition is vacuous. Then the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(\sum_{i=1}^r f_ix_i))$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Reducedness of this quotient is not asserted.

proof.text: Put B=A[x_i], L=∑ f_i x_i and I=(L). Finite type over the field makes A Noetherian, hence B is Noetherian. Polynomial rings over domains are domains.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, lemma-bertini-irreducible, middle proof paragraph (affine incidence hypersurface and codimension-two base locus), lines 9089--9132

proof.text: For any domain R and coefficients with f_j a unit, the linear form L is prime in R[x_i]. Write t=∑_{i≠j} f_i x_i. The substitutions x_j↦f_j x_j+t and x_j↦f_j⁻¹(x_j−t), fixing all other variables, are inverse R-algebra automorphisms: both fix t and the two composites send x_j to itself. The first sends the prime element x_j to L, so L is prime and (L) is a prime ideal. This is the proved private helper linear_prime_of_unit, using Mathlib MvPolynomial.X_prime and MulEquiv.prime_iff.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, lemma-bertini-irreducible, middle proof paragraph (affine incidence hypersurface and codimension-two base locus), lines 9089--9132

proof.text: Let Q be minimal over I. Krull’s principal ideal theorem, the direct Mathlib corollary of the height-of-a-principal-quotient bound, gives ht(Q)≤1. The polynomial algebra is free and hence flat over A. The flat height formula gives ht(Q)≥ht(Q∩A). If every coefficient belonged to Q, then J⊆Q∩A; a prime p₀ minimal over J below Q∩A would have height at least two by hypothesis, contradicting ht(Q)≤1. Hence some f_j is outside Q. This includes J=A, since no proper contracted prime contains A.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, lemma-bertini-irreducible, middle proof paragraph (affine incidence hypersurface and codimension-two base locus), lines 9089--9132

proof.text: Localize A at f_j for a coefficient outside Q. This coefficient is nonzero, so S=A[1/f_j] is a domain and A→S is injective. The ring S[x_i] is the localization of B at the powers of C(f_j). By step 2 the extended ideal IS[x_i] is prime. Since Q avoids the denominators, contraction of its extension is Q. Thus I⊆(IS[x_i]∩B)⊆Q, and minimality of Q identifies Q with this prime contraction. If C(a) belongs to Q, its image is a multiple of L over S[x_i]. Taking constant coefficients gives a/1=0; injectivity gives a=0. Hence Q∩A=0. The localization contraction theorem implements clearing denominators, without constructing a separate evaluation kernel.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, lemma-bertini-irreducible, middle proof paragraph (affine incidence hypersurface and codimension-two base locus), lines 9089--9132

proof.text: Let K=Frac(A). Fix an index j with f_j≠0. In K[x_i] the ideal generated by L is prime by step 2; call its contraction P. Every minimal prime Q over I avoids every nonzero constant by step 4. Apply the same localization contraction and minimality argument, now at all nonzero elements of A, to get Q=P. There is at least one such Q by existence of a minimal prime inside P. Therefore the minimal-prime set of I is the singleton {P}, and √I=P. Its image in B/I is the nilradical, which is prime. The Mathlib irreducible-spectrum/nilradical criterion proves Spec(B/I) irreducible, without asserting reducedness.
